evidence: Hor. S. 1.1.120–121: verbum nōn amplius addam
terms.comment: Ūnō verbō, in a word (Cic. Fin. 2.73); ad verbum, word for word (Cic. Fin. 1.4); meīs verbīs, from me, in my name (Cic. Att. 16.11.8). For verba dare see word, promise.

terms.gloss: a word as the name of a thing
evidence: Gell. 4.1.18: rem nōn suō vocābulō dēmōnstrāre
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “an appellation, designation, name of any thing”.

terms.gloss: a word as spoken, a saying; voice
evidence: Cic. Fin. 2.6 (Lewis & Short): quid sonet haec vōx voluptātis

phrases.latin: jam satis est. … verbum nōn amplius addam
phrases.english: That’s enough now. … I won’t add another word.

phrases.latin: nōndum prīma verba exprimit, jam coccum intellegit, jam conchȳlium poscit.
phrases.english: He can’t say his first words yet, but he already knows scarlet and asks for purple.

phrases.latin: hās prīmum audiet puer, hārum verba effingere imitandō cōnābitur
phrases.english: these the child will hear first, and theirs are the words he will try to copy

sources: Lewis & Short: verbum · Lewis & Short: vocabulum · Lewis & Short: vox
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-horatius, loci-quintilianus, loci-terentius, loci-gellius, loci-cicero-epistulae), as checked there against the editions they name.
